 Governor Bryan Announces Automatic SNAP Relief for 3,755 Households Affected by Power Outages
 Search Latest Comments
 No comments to show. 
 November 9 
 Governor also announces federal approval of 18 Opportunity Zones, major progress on Veterans Drive Phase 2 and a new initiative to accelerate payments to government vendors. 
 U.S. VIRGIN ISLANDS — Governor Albert Bryan Jr. announced Monday that 3,755 households on St. Thomas and St. John have received automatic replacement Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits following the prolonged power outages in late October, providing much-needed relief to families who lost food during the electrical disruptions.
 The replacement benefits were deposited directly onto eligible households’ Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) cards Saturday, Nov. 7, following federal approval of a request by the Bryan-Roach Administration to waive the normal application and affidavit requirements for food replacement assistance.
 During his weekly Government House press briefing, Governor Bryan said the administration worked proactively through the Virgin Islands Department of Human Services to secure authorization from the U.S. Department of Agriculture, allowing affected households to receive replacement benefits equal to 30% of their previous month’s SNAP allotment without submitting individual applications.
 “For families already struggling to make ends meet, losing a refrigerator full of groceries is a serious financial burden,” Governor Bryan said. “We didn’t want people standing in lines or filling out paperwork to replace food they lost because of the outages. We went to the federal government, requested the assistance and got it directly onto their EBT cards.”
 The Governor thanked Human Services Commissioner Averil George and her team for their swift response, while acknowledging the continuing need to improve electrical reliability throughout the territory.
 Governor Bryan also announced significant progress on the Veterans Drive Phase 2 Improvement Project, federal approval of all 18 Opportunity Zones nominated by his administration and a new initiative to help government vendors receive payments more quickly.
 Major Federal Agreement Advances Veterans Drive Phase 2 
 Governor Bryan announced that the Government of the Virgin Islands has reached a critical agreement with the U.S. Coast Guard to advance Phase 2 of the Veterans Drive Improvement Project on St. Thomas, removing a longstanding federal property obstacle and bringing the approximately $100 million waterfront improvement project closer to construction.
 The agreement represents a significant step toward completing the transformation of the Charlotte Amalie waterfront, building on the first phase of the project completed in 2021.
 The second phase will expand the roadway around the Legislature to four lanes, create a tree-lined pedestrian promenade, improve drainage and strengthen the seawall to better protect the waterfront and surrounding downtown area.
 The agreement follows extensive coordination among the Bryan-Roach Administration, the U.S. Coast Guard, the Federal Highway Administration, Eastern Federal Lands and the Virgin Islands departments of Public Works and Property and Procurement.
 The project’s pre-solicitation period is underway through Nov. 19, with the solicitation period continuing through Jan. 13, 2027. Final property surveys, appraisals and other required approvals remain outstanding.
 “This is a project the people of St. Thomas have been waiting a long time to see move forward, and we’ve worked hard to get to this point,” Governor Bryan said. “When we completed the first phase of Veterans Drive, we showed what was possible for our waterfront. Now we’re clearing the way for the next phase. We’re not going to finish every project before we leave office, but we can make sure the next administration has something solid to build on. That’s how government is supposed to work.”
 The Governor also cited continued progress on Mahogany Road, Nardo Trotman Drive, Spring Gut Road and the Paul E. Joseph Stadium, noting that those projects are nearing completion, underway or expected to begin within the next 60 days.
 Federal Approval Creates New Opportunities for Private Investment 
 In another significant economic development announcement, Governor Bryan confirmed that the U.S. Department of the Treasury has approved all 18 census tracts submitted by the administration for federal Opportunity Zone designation.
 The designations include nine tracts on St. Croix, eight on St. Thomas and one on St. John. All 18 qualify as rural Opportunity Zones, providing additional federal tax incentives intended to encourage private investment in eligible communities.
 On St. Croix, the approved areas include portions of Christiansted, Frederiksted, Kingshill and the South Shore, including the former HOVENSA refinery and Renaissance properties. Their inclusion supports the administration’s broader efforts to attract manufacturing, energy development and international trade investment.
 On St. Thomas, the designated areas include Tutu, Anna’s Retreat, Smith Bay, Crown Bay, Havensight and Charlotte Amalie. Cruz Bay and surrounding communities on St. John are included for the first time.
 The designations take effect Jan. 1, 2027, and remain in place for 10 years.
 “Government cannot build this economy by itself,” Governor Bryan said. “We’ve spent eight years improving our infrastructure and creating opportunities for investment. These designations give us another advantage in attracting businesses, developing housing and creating jobs. But getting the designation is only the beginning. What matters is turning those opportunities into real investments that benefit Virgin Islanders.”
 The Governor credited the Virgin Islands Economic Development Authority and other government partners for their work in securing the approvals.
 New Initiative Offers Government Vendors Faster Payments 
 Governor Bryan also announced a partnership with Municipal Vendor Services Inc. (MVSI) that will allow businesses providing goods and services to the Government of the Virgin Islands to receive payments in as little as 72 hours after their invoices have been approved.
 The voluntary initiative is designed to address longstanding concerns about government payment delays, particularly among small businesses that depend on timely payments to meet payroll, purchase supplies and cover operating expenses.
 The program will also provide the government with additional flexibility in managing its cash flow.
 “When you’re running a business, you have employees to pay and bills coming due. You can’t tell your employees to wait until the government pays you,” Governor Bryan said. “We know our payment cycles have been a challenge. This gives our vendors another option and helps make it easier to do business with the government.”
 Additional information about vendor enrollment and participation will be released.
